title: Quadratic Trigonometric Equations
subject: mathematics

theory.introduction: Some trigonometric equations have the form of quadratic equations when one trigonometric function is treated as the variable.

content.text: If an equation contains repeated powers of one trigonometric function, temporarily treat that function as a variable and solve the resulting quadratic.
After solving the quadratic, substitute the trigonometric expression back and solve the resulting trigonometric equations.

formulas.name: Quadratic Form
formulas.explanation: A repeated trigonometric expression can sometimes be represented by u and solved as a quadratic.

examples.question: Solve 2cos²(x) − 3cos(x) + 1 = 0.
examples.solution: Let u = cos(x). Then 2u² − 3u + 1 = 0, which factors as (2u − 1)(u − 1) = 0. Therefore cos(x) = 1/2 or cos(x) = 1. Solve each equation separately.

key_ideas: Convert every algebraic solution back into an angle.
misconceptions: Forgetting to check whether the obtained trigonometric values are possible.
